subject: Week 45: respond to every point — gestures are the pre-word signal
bodyText:
This week
Days 313–319: cruising for many, first independent steps for early walkers — the range for first steps runs roughly 9 to 15+ months, with the CDC walks-alone checkpoint at 15 months (https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). Comprehension is running well ahead of speech: he searches for fully hidden objects, uses objects functionally, and shows the full emotional range; first words are emerging for some, with the CDC 2022 checkpoint for words beyond mama/dada at 15 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Clinginess and pickier eating — a toddler-style behavior dip that passes on its own.
- [monitor] Sustained milestone absence across multiple domains at once (motor plus language plus social); single-domain lag on its own is usually timing variance.
- [call within 24h] Persistent illness, or reduced intake with noticeably fewer wet diapers.
- [call now] Severe respiratory distress — retractions, grunting, blue lips — or fever ≥102°F rectal with lethargy — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Respond to every point with a three-beat loop — follow the point, name the thing, expand by one attribute (dog; big brown dog). Conversational turns, not raw word count, drive the language-network effect. Romeo et al. 2018 (PubMed): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Clear a barefoot walking runway — 8–10 feet of clutter-free floor between two stable anchors — and let him launch on his own; hands-free practice beats hand-walking for balance learning, whether first steps come this month or at 15 months. AAP: Movement 8 to 12 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Start the year-1 photo book now rather than birthday week — Artifact Uprising, Mixbook, and Chatbooks all handle 12-month layouts; an hour a week from here finishes it without a deadline scramble.
- Shift part of read-aloud time to point-and-name board books and let him drive the page turns — following his attention is what dialogic reading looks like at this age. Reach Out and Read: https://reachoutandread.org/

Upcoming
- Day 344–351 (Apr 20–27, 2027): cake-order window — custom bakeries want 2–3 weeks of lead for a May 11 pickup.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — RSVPs out this week if they are not already; schedule the party for late morning or after the second nap, and protect both naps on the day.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Stands alone for a few seconds
  AAP window: day 300-365
  What to look for: Often follows cruising. Balance precedes locomotion.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stands-briefly-no-support/complete

- Uses objects appropriately (cup, phone, book)
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Functional use — picks up phone and puts it to ear, holds book the right way. Pretend play emerges from here.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-objects-appropriately/complete

- Takes a few steps on her own
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: CDC checkpoint is 15 months. Wide normal range — late walking alone is not concerning if other milestones are on track.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-independent-steps/complete

- Uses one word besides mama or dada
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Commonly 'ball', 'dog', 'bye', or a family-specific word.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-one-word/complete

- Tries to imitate words you say
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Approximations count. 'Wa' for water is a real attempt.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tries-to-imitate-words/complete
